ZWE: The ancient stone city of Great Zimbabwe was built without any cement, and the country is named after it.
Hwange National Park is home to huge herds of elephants that gather at its watering holes.
ZMB: Victoria Falls is so loud and misty that its local name, Mosi-oa-Tunya, means 'the smoke that thunders'.
Every year, millions of fruit bats fly into Kasanka National Park, one of the biggest animal gatherings on Earth.
YEM: On Socotra Island grow dragon's blood trees, which look like giant umbrellas and have deep red sap.
In the old town of Shibam, people built tall tower houses out of mud bricks hundreds of years ago.
VNM: Son Doong is the biggest known cave in the world, so huge that a jungle grows inside it!
Pho is a famous Vietnamese noodle soup, often slurped for breakfast with fresh herbs and a squeeze of lime.
VEN: Angel Falls is the tallest waterfall in the world, tumbling off the edge of a flat-topped mountain.
Arepas are round corn cakes that people love to stuff with cheese, beans or meat.
VAT: Vatican City is the smallest country in the world, so tiny you could walk across it in less than half an hour.
Michelangelo spent about four years painting the giant ceiling of the Sistine Chapel here.
VUT: Vanuatu is a chain of more than 80 islands, shaped a bit like the letter Y.
On Tanna Island, visitors can peek into Mount Yasur, a volcano that puffs out glowing red lava.
UZB: Samarkand, an old Silk Road city, has dazzling buildings covered in bright blue tiles.
Uzbekistan is doubly landlocked: every country around it also has no ocean coast.
URY: The very first football World Cup was played in Uruguay, way back in 1930.
On a beach in Punta del Este, giant stone fingers poke out of the sand, as if a hand is waving hello.
FSM: On the island of Yap, people used giant stone discs, some taller than a grown-up, as money.
Nan Madol is an ancient city built on dozens of small human-made islands, linked by water channels.
MHL: These islands are coral atolls, rings of low, sandy land wrapped around calm blue lagoons.
Long ago, Marshallese sailors made maps of ocean waves using sticks and shells tied together.
MNP: Latte stones, tall stone pillars topped with round caps, once held up the houses of the Chamorro people here.
On Saipan, divers swim into the Grotto, a cave pool where sunlight makes the water glow blue.
VIR: At Trunk Bay on St. John, an underwater snorkel trail has signs that tell you about the coral and fish.
During carnival, dancers called moko jumbies parade on very tall stilts in bright costumes.
GUM: Guam is nicknamed 'Where America's Day Begins' because each new day starts there hours before mainland America.
The Mariana Trench, the deepest part of all the oceans, lies in the sea not far from Guam.
ASM: Big fruit bats called flying foxes glide over the rainforests of the National Park of American Samoa.
Rose Atoll, a tiny ring of coral, is the southernmost point of the United States.
PRI: In some bays, the water sparkles blue at night when you swish your hand, thanks to tiny glowing creatures.
A tiny tree frog called the coquí sings 'ko-KEE' every night and is a much-loved island symbol.
USA: Yellowstone was the world's first national park, and its geysers shoot hot water high into the air.
The Statue of Liberty was a gift from France, and her copper skin slowly turned green.
SGS: Huge crowds of king penguins live on South Georgia's beaches, all squawking and waddling together.
Wandering albatrosses nest here, and they have the widest wingspan of any bird alive today.
IOT: The Chagos Archipelago is a group of coral atolls sitting in the middle of the Indian Ocean.
Coconut crabs, the biggest crabs that live on land, scuttle around these islands.
SHN: Jacob's Ladder is a staircase of 699 steps that climbs straight up a steep hill.
Whale sharks, the biggest fish in the sea, visit the warm waters around Saint Helena.
PCN: Of the four Pitcairn Islands, only Pitcairn Island itself has people living on it.
Henderson Island is home to the Henderson crake, a little black bird that cannot fly.
AIA: Anguilla's name comes from an old word for 'eel', maybe because the island is long and thin.
Boat racing is the national sport, and colourful sailboats race along the island's coast.
FLK: Five kinds of penguins nest on these windswept islands, including kings, gentoos and rockhoppers.
Most of the world's black-browed albatrosses build their nests on these islands.
CYM: At Stingray City, gentle stingrays glide right up to visitors standing in shallow, sandy water.
Blue iguanas, big lizards with bluish skin, live only on Grand Cayman.
BMU: Bermuda's beaches have pink sand, coloured by the shells of tiny red sea creatures.
Houses here have white stepped roofs that catch rainwater for people to use.
VGB: At The Baths on Virgin Gorda, giant granite boulders form secret caves and pools along the beach.
Anegada is a flat island made of coral, unlike the hilly islands around it.
TCA: The Turks Islands are said to be named after a cactus whose red top looks like a fez hat.
Every winter, humpback whales swim past these islands on their long ocean journey.
MSR: Montserrat is nicknamed 'the Emerald Isle of the Caribbean' for its green hills and Irish links.
The Montserrat oriole, a black and yellow songbird, lives nowhere else in the world.
JEY: Jersey cows, with big dark eyes and light brown coats, first came from this island.
The sea around Jersey has some of the biggest tides in the world, uncovering huge rocky shores at low tide.
GGY: Guernsey cows, golden and white, come from this island and are famous for their rich, creamy milk.
On nearby Sark, cars aren't allowed, so people get around by bike, horse and cart, or tractor.
IMN: Manx cats from the Isle of Man are famous for having no tail at all, or just a stubby one.
The Laxey Wheel is a giant red waterwheel, one of the largest working waterwheels in the world.
GBR: The United Kingdom is made up of four nations: England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland.
London's Underground, nicknamed the Tube, is the oldest underground railway in the world.
ARE: When the Burj Khalifa in Dubai was finished, it became the tallest building ever built, over 800 metres high.
Falcons are the national bird, and Abu Dhabi even has a special hospital just for falcons.
UKR: Huge golden fields of sunflowers stretch across Ukraine in summer.
Pysanky are eggs decorated with beautiful patterns made using beeswax and bright dyes.
UGA: Mountain gorillas live in Uganda's misty Bwindi Impenetrable Forest.
At Jinja, the River Nile flows out of Lake Victoria and begins its long trip north to Egypt.
TKM: Akhal-Teke horses from Turkmenistan have shiny coats that can shimmer like gold.
Most of the land is covered by the Karakum Desert, whose name means 'black sand'.
TUR: In Cappadocia, hot air balloons float over strange rock towers called fairy chimneys.
Istanbul is built on two continents, with part of the city in Europe and part in Asia.
TUN: In Matmata, some homes are dug into the ground, and one became Luke Skywalker's home in Star Wars.
The northernmost point of all of Africa is on Tunisia's coast.
TTO: The steelpan, a drum made from an oil barrel, was invented in Trinidad and Tobago.
Pitch Lake is the largest natural lake of asphalt in the world, the gooey black stuff used on roads.
TON: Humpback whales swim to Tonga's warm waters each year to have their babies.
Ha'amonga 'a Maui is an ancient stone gateway made of three huge coral stones.
TGO: In Koutammakou, the Batammariba people build mud tower houses that look like little castles.
Togo is long and thin, with only a short coastline on the Gulf of Guinea.
TLS: An old legend says the island of Timor was once a kind crocodile that turned into land.
The sea around Atauro Island is packed with colourful corals and reef fish.
THA: The elephant is Thailand's national animal and an important symbol of the country.
At floating markets, people sell fruit, noodles and snacks straight from their boats.
TZA: Mount Kilimanjaro is the tallest mountain in Africa, with snow on top even though it's near the equator.
Every year, huge herds of wildebeest and zebras travel across the Serengeti in the Great Migration.
TJK: The Pamir Mountains, which cover much of Tajikistan, are nicknamed 'the Roof of the World'.
Marco Polo sheep, with giant curly horns, roam the high mountain valleys.
TWN: Taroko Gorge has towering marble cliffs carved out by a rushing river.
Formosan black bears live in the island's mountain forests and have a white V-shaped mark on their chests.
SYR: Damascus is one of the oldest cities in the world, where people have lived for thousands of years.
Aleppo soap, made with olive oil and laurel oil, has been made by hand for centuries.
CHE: Switzerland has four national languages: German, French, Italian and Romansh.
The holes in Swiss Emmental cheese come from tiny gas bubbles that form as the cheese ripens.
SWE: Every winter in northern Sweden, artists build a hotel out of ice and snow.
Thanks to the 'right to roam', anyone in Sweden can hike and camp in nature, as long as they take care of it.
SWZ: Eswatini is a small landlocked country tucked between South Africa and Mozambique.
Rhinos, elephants and lions roam in Hlane Royal National Park.
SUR: Suriname is the smallest country in South America, and Dutch is its official language.
Thick rainforest covers most of the land, full of monkeys, jaguars and colourful birds.
SDS: The Sudd is one of the biggest swamps in the world, formed by the White Nile River.
Huge herds of antelope, like white-eared kob, travel across South Sudan's grasslands every year.
SDN: Sudan has more pyramids than Egypt, built long ago by the kings and queens of Kush.
In Khartoum, the Blue Nile and the White Nile meet and join to become one great river.
LKA: Sigiriya is a giant rock with an ancient palace on top, and huge stone lion paws guard the stairs.
Ceylon tea, grown on Sri Lanka's misty green hills, is enjoyed all around the world.
ESP: At the La Tomatina festival, people throw squishy tomatoes at each other just for fun!
The Alhambra in Granada is a palace famous for its beautiful patterned tiles and splashing fountains.
KOR: Kimchi, a spicy dish of fermented cabbage, is served with almost every Korean meal.
Hangul, the Korean alphabet, was invented almost 600 years ago to be easy for everyone to learn.
ZAF: Table Mountain in Cape Town has a flat top that often gets covered by a 'tablecloth' of clouds.
At Boulders Beach, African penguins waddle across the sand and swim in the sea.
SOM: Somalia has the longest coastline of any country on mainland Africa.
Camels are very important here, and camel milk is a popular drink.
SOL: This land on the Horn of Africa stretches along the Gulf of Aden, with dry mountains and wide plains.
Near Hargeisa, the Laas Geel caves have ancient rock paintings of cows in bright colours.
SLB: Marovo Lagoon is a huge lagoon dotted with hundreds of small, jungle-covered islands.
On some islands, shell money made of tiny polished shells on long strings is still used.
SVK: Spiš Castle is one of the biggest castle sites in Central Europe, sitting high on a hill.
The High Tatras are the tallest part of the Carpathian Mountains, with sparkling mountain lakes.
SVN: Lake Bled has a tiny island with a church on it, and you reach it by wooden rowing boat.
Postojna Cave is home to the olm, a pale salamander nicknamed the 'baby dragon'.
SGP: The Merlion, half lion and half fish, is Singapore's famous symbol.
Gardens by the Bay has giant 'Supertrees' covered in plants that light up at night.
SLE: The name Sierra Leone means 'Lion Mountains', given by sailors who saw its hills from the sea.
Tiwai Island is a forest island home to many kinds of monkeys.
SYC: The coco de mer palm grows the biggest seed of any plant in the world.
Aldabra Atoll is home to a huge number of giant tortoises.
SRB: Belgrade, the capital, sits right where two rivers, the Sava and the Danube, meet.
Serbia is famous for growing lots of juicy raspberries.
SEN: Lake Retba, also called the Pink Lake, gets its colour from tiny salt-loving algae.
The westernmost point of mainland Africa is near Dakar, Senegal's capital.
SAU: The Rub' al Khali, or Empty Quarter, is the biggest stretch of sand desert in the world.
Near AlUla stands Elephant Rock, a giant sandstone rock shaped just like an elephant.
STP: The equator runs across Ilhéu das Rolas, a tiny island where a marker shows the line.
Pico Cão Grande is a giant needle of volcanic rock poking up out of the jungle.
SMR: San Marino is completely surrounded by Italy and is one of the smallest countries in Europe.
Three towers on top of Mount Titano appear on San Marino's coat of arms.
WSM: Samoa is one of the first places on Earth to greet each new day.
On Savai'i island, blowholes shoot seawater high into the air like giant fountains.
VCT: The country is the island of Saint Vincent plus a string of small islands called the Grenadines.
The Saint Vincent parrot, with gold, green and purple feathers, lives only on this island.
LCA: The Pitons are two pointy volcanic mountains that rise straight up from the sea.
Near Soufrière, you can visit a volcano area with bubbling mud pools and warm springs.
KNA: Saint Kitts and Nevis is the smallest country in the Americas.
Green vervet monkeys are a common sight on the islands.
RWA: Rwanda is called the 'Land of a Thousand Hills' because it is so hilly.
Playful golden monkeys swing through the bamboo forests of Volcanoes National Park.
RUS: Russia is the biggest country in the world and stretches across 11 time zones.
Lake Baikal is the deepest lake on Earth, and cute freshwater seals called nerpas live there.
ROU: Great white pelicans and hundreds of other kinds of birds live in the Danube Delta.
Salina Turda is an old salt mine turned into an underground park, with a Ferris wheel inside!
QAT: Qatar is a peninsula that sticks out into the Gulf, a bit like a thumb.
At Khor Al Adaid, the 'inland sea', golden sand dunes roll right down to the water.
PRT: Portugal is famous for cork, which comes from the bark of cork oak trees and grows back.
Pastéis de nata are little custard tarts with crispy pastry, first made in Lisbon.
POL: Deep in the Wieliczka Salt Mine, even the chandeliers are carved out of salt.
Pierogi are dumplings stuffed with potato, cheese, or even fruit.
PHL: The Philippines is made up of more than 7,000 islands.
The Chocolate Hills in Bohol turn brown in the dry season, like giant chocolate drops.
PER: Machu Picchu is an ancient Inca city perched high up in the Andes Mountains.
Potatoes were first grown in the Andes, and Peru has thousands of different kinds.
PRY: Most people in Paraguay speak two languages: Spanish and Guaraní, a native language.
The Gran Chaco is a hot, wild land where giant anteaters and armadillos live.
PNG: More than 800 languages are spoken in Papua New Guinea, more than in any other country.
Birds of paradise, with amazing colourful feathers, dance in the rainforests.
PAN: The Panama Canal lets ships cross between the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans without sailing around South America.
Because of Panama's curvy shape, from some spots you can watch the sun rise over the Pacific Ocean.
PLW: Palau's Rock Islands are hundreds of green, mushroom-shaped islands in a turquoise lagoon.
Manta rays, sea turtles and giant clams live among the coral reefs.
PAK: Mohenjo-daro is an ancient city over 4,000 years old, with brick houses and even drains.
Pink 'Himalayan' salt actually comes from the Khewra Salt Mine in Pakistan.
OMN: Frankincense trees grow in Oman, and their sweet-smelling sap has been traded for thousands of years.
Green sea turtles crawl onto the beach at Ras al Jinz to lay their eggs.
NOR: Norway's coast has deep, narrow sea inlets called fjords, carved by glaciers long ago.
In the far north, the sun doesn't set for weeks in summer, so Norway is called the land of the midnight sun.
PRK: Mount Paektu is a volcano with a deep blue crater lake called Heaven Lake on top.
Naengmyeon, a bowl of cold buckwheat noodles, is a famous dish in North Korea.
NGA: Jollof rice, cooked in a rich tomato and pepper sauce, is a favourite party dish.
Zuma Rock is a giant rock near Abuja, with markings that look like a face.
NER: West African giraffes, with pale patchy coats, roam near the village of Kouré.
The mud-brick tower of the Agadez Mosque is one of the tallest mud buildings in the world.
NIC: Nicaragua is called the 'land of lakes and volcanoes'.
Lake Nicaragua is one of the few lakes where sharks live, swimming up a river from the sea.
NZL: The kiwi is a fluffy brown bird that can't fly and comes out at night.
In the Waitomo Caves, thousands of tiny glowworms light up the ceiling like stars.
NIU: Niue is one of the biggest raised coral islands in the world, nicknamed 'The Rock'.
Humpback whales visit, and sometimes you can spot them right from the shore.
COK: Aitutaki has a huge turquoise lagoon dotted with tiny sandy islands.
Rarotonga is so small that you can drive all the way around it in under an hour.
NLD: About a quarter of the Netherlands lies below sea level, kept dry by dikes and pumps.
In spring, colourful tulip fields stretch across the land, often with windmills nearby.
ABW: Aruba's divi-divi trees all lean the same way, bent by the steady trade winds.
People here speak Papiamento, a language that mixes Spanish, Portuguese, Dutch and African words.
CUW: In Willemstad, houses along the waterfront are painted in bright candy colours.
The Queen Emma Bridge floats on boats and swings open to let ships pass.
NPL: Mount Everest, the highest mountain on Earth, sits on the border between Nepal and China.
Nepal's flag is the only national flag in the world that isn't a rectangle.
NRU: Nauru is the smallest island country in the world.
Unlike most countries, Nauru has no official capital city.
NAM: Sossusvlei has some of the tallest sand dunes in the world, glowing red and orange in the sun.
The Hoba meteorite, the biggest known meteorite on Earth, landed in Namibia long ago.
MOZ: Dugongs, gentle 'sea cows' that munch sea grass, live around the Bazaruto Islands.
Matapa is a dish made from cassava leaves cooked with peanuts and coconut milk.
MAR: Chefchaouen is a mountain town where many buildings are painted in shades of blue.
Goats in Morocco climb right up into argan trees to nibble the fruit!
SAH: This desert land faces the Atlantic Ocean, where the Sahara meets the sea.
Camels with one hump, called dromedaries, roam across its rocky plains and sand dunes.
MNE: Montenegro means 'black mountain', after its dark, forest-covered mountains.
The Bay of Kotor is a winding bay hugged by steep mountains, a bit like a fjord.
MNG: Many families in Mongolia live in round felt tents called gers that can be packed up and moved.
Dinosaur eggs were discovered at the Flaming Cliffs in the Gobi Desert.
MDA: At Orheiul Vechi, monks carved rooms into a limestone cliff above a looping river.
Plăcinte are tasty pies stuffed with cheese, potatoes or cabbage.
MCO: Monaco is the second-smallest country in the world, after Vatican City.
The Monaco Grand Prix is a famous car race that zooms through the city's narrow streets.
MEX: Corn was first grown in Mexico thousands of years ago, and it's still used to make tortillas.
Every winter, millions of monarch butterflies fly to Mexico's mountain forests.
MUS: At Chamarel, the Seven Coloured Earth is a patch of sand dunes in red, purple, brown and yellow.
Off the coast near Le Morne, sand flowing underwater looks just like a giant underwater waterfall.
MRT: The Eye of the Sahara is a giant ring of rocks in the desert, so big it can be seen from space.
One of the longest trains in the world rumbles across Mauritania's desert carrying iron ore.
MLT: Malta's ancient stone temples are older than the pyramids of Egypt.
The Blue Grotto is a group of sea caves where the water glows bright blue.
MLI: The Great Mosque of Djenné is the largest mud-brick building in the world, and townspeople replaster it together every year.
Timbuktu was once a great city of learning, and many old handwritten books are kept there.
MDV: The Maldives is the lowest country in the world, mostly just a metre or two above the sea.
More than a thousand coral islands make up the Maldives, grouped into rings called atolls.
MYS: Orangutans, whose name means 'person of the forest', live in Malaysia's rainforests on Borneo.
The Petronas Twin Towers in Kuala Lumpur are joined by a sky bridge high above the ground.
MWI: Lake Malawi has more kinds of fish than any other lake in the world.
Malawi is nicknamed 'the Warm Heart of Africa' because its people are so friendly.
MDG: Madagascar is the home of lemurs, big-eyed animals found almost nowhere else on Earth.
The Avenue of the Baobabs is a road lined with giant trees that look like they're growing upside down.
MKD: Lake Ohrid is one of the oldest and deepest lakes in Europe.
Tavče gravče, beans baked in a clay pot, is a favourite national dish.
LUX: Luxembourg is the only Grand Duchy left in the world.
The Mullerthal region is called 'Little Switzerland' for its rocky forests and streams.
LTU: The Curonian Spit is a long, thin strip of sand dunes between a lagoon and the Baltic Sea.
Cepelinai are big potato dumplings named after zeppelin airships because of their shape.
LIE: Liechtenstein has no seaside, and neither do its only two neighbours, Switzerland and Austria.
This country is so small and narrow that you could walk across it in an afternoon.
LBY: Most of Libya is covered by the Sahara Desert.
In the old town of Ghadames, houses are joined by shady covered alleys that stay cool in the desert heat.
LBR: Pygmy hippos, small shy hippos about the size of a big pig, live in Liberia's forests.
Liberia's flag looks a lot like the US flag, but it has just one big white star.
LSO: Even the lowest point in Lesotho is over 1,000 metres high, higher than any other country's lowest point.
Many Basotho people wear colourful wool blankets and cone-shaped straw hats.
LBN: A green cedar tree is the symbol in the middle of Lebanon's flag.
In Jeita Grotto, you can take a boat ride through a cave full of amazing rock shapes.
LVA: About half of Latvia is covered in forest.
Riga is famous for its fancy Art Nouveau buildings, decorated with stone faces and creatures.
LAO: Kuang Si Falls tumbles down through the jungle into pools of turquoise water.
Sticky rice is a favourite food in Laos, often rolled into little balls and eaten with your fingers.
KGZ: Issyk-Kul is a huge mountain lake that never freezes, even in the cold winter.
The flag shows the round top of a yurt, the felt tents many families use in summer.
KWT: The Kuwait Towers stand by the sea, and two of them have big balls decorated with shiny blue and green discs.
Machboos, spiced rice cooked with meat or fish, is a favourite dish in Kuwait.
KOS: The Rugova Gorge is a deep, dramatic canyon in the mountains, great for hiking.
The Mirusha Waterfalls tumble down in steps, linking a chain of little lakes.
KIR: Kiribati is the only country that is in all four hemispheres: north, south, east and west.
Kiritimati, part of Kiribati, is the largest coral atoll in the world by land.
KEN: The Great Rift Valley, a giant crack in the Earth's surface, runs right through Kenya.
Huge flocks of pink flamingos often gather on Kenya's lakes.
KAZ: Kazakhstan is the largest landlocked country in the world.
Apples first came from wild apple forests in Kazakhstan, near the city of Almaty.
JOR: Petra is an ancient city carved right into pinkish-red rock cliffs.
The Dead Sea is so salty that you float on top of the water without even trying!
JPN: Mount Fuji, Japan's tallest mountain, is a snowy volcano shaped like a cone.
Japan's bullet trains, called Shinkansen, zoom across the country at super high speeds.
JAM: At Dunn's River Falls, visitors can climb right up the waterfall like a giant staircase.
Ackee and saltfish is Jamaica's national dish, and cooked ackee looks a lot like scrambled eggs.
ITA: Venice is a city built on water, where people get around by boat along canals.
Pizza as we know it was first made in the Italian city of Naples.
ISR: Makhtesh Ramon is a giant crater in the Negev Desert, carved out by water and wind, not a meteorite.
In winter, thousands of cranes stop to rest and feed in the Hula Valley.
PSX: Jericho, in the Jordan Valley, is one of the oldest cities in the world and the lowest city on Earth.
Olive trees grow on the rocky hills, and some of them are hundreds of years old.
IRL: Puffins nest on the Cliffs of Moher, which rise high above the Atlantic Ocean.
Ireland has no native wild snakes, not a single kind.
IRQ: Some of the world's first writing was invented here long ago, by pressing marks into clay tablets.
In the marshes of southern Iraq, people build giant houses made only from woven reeds.
IRN: Persian carpets, woven by hand with beautiful patterns, are famous around the world.
Iran grows most of the world's saffron, a precious red spice that comes from crocus flowers.
IDN: Komodo dragons, the biggest lizards in the world, live on a few Indonesian islands.
Indonesia is made up of thousands of islands, stretching across the sea between Asia and Australia.
IND: India is the only country where both wild lions and wild tigers live.
Chess grew from an old Indian game called chaturanga, played over a thousand years ago.
ISL: A hot spring in Iceland called Geysir gave its name to all the geysers in the world.
Every summer, puffins with bright orange beaks nest on Iceland's sea cliffs.
HUN: The Rubik's Cube was invented in Hungary by Ernő Rubik.
Lake Balaton is the largest lake in Central Europe.
HND: Copán is an ancient Maya city with a giant stone staircase covered in carvings.
Whale sharks, the biggest fish in the sea, swim near the Bay Islands.
HTI: Haiti's name comes from a Taíno word meaning 'land of high mountains'.
Soup joumou, a warm pumpkin soup, is a special dish eaten on New Year's Day.
GUY: Kaieteur Falls is one of the most powerful single-drop waterfalls in the world.
The giant water lily, Guyana's national flower, has huge round leaves that float on the water.
GNB: In the Bijagós Islands, hippos swim in the salty sea instead of just in rivers.
Lots of cashew nuts are grown in Guinea-Bissau.
GIN: Guinea is called the 'water tower of West Africa' because big rivers, like the Niger, start in its hills.
The Nimba toad, found on Mount Nimba, gives birth to baby toads instead of laying eggs.
GTM: Tikal is an ancient Maya city whose tall stone pyramids poke above the rainforest.
The quetzal, a bird with long shiny green tail feathers, is the national bird and gives its name to the money.
GRD: Grenada is called the 'Spice Isle', and a nutmeg is even pictured on its flag.
Off its coast, an underwater sculpture park has statues that have become homes for coral and fish.
GRC: The first Olympic Games were held long ago at Olympia in ancient Greece.
Greece has thousands of islands, and many have white houses with blue doors and domes.
GHA: Kente cloth, woven in bright strips of colourful patterns, comes from Ghana.
Lake Volta is one of the largest human-made lakes in the world.
DEU: Neuschwanstein Castle looks so magical that it is said to have inspired Disney's Sleeping Beauty castle.
The Brothers Grimm, who collected fairy tales like Snow White and Hansel and Gretel, were German.
GEO: Khachapuri is a boat-shaped bread filled with melted cheese and an egg on top.
Ushguli, high in the Caucasus Mountains, is one of the highest villages in Europe where people live all year.
GMB: The Gambia is the smallest country on mainland Africa, a thin strip along the Gambia River.
Chimpanzees live on islands in the River Gambia National Park.
GAB: In Loango National Park, hippos, elephants and buffalo sometimes stroll along the beach.
Most of Gabon is covered in rainforest.
FRA: The Eiffel Tower in Paris was built for a world fair in 1889.
Croissants, flaky crescent-shaped pastries, are a favourite French breakfast.
SPM: These small French islands lie in the Atlantic Ocean, just off the coast of Canada.
Miquelon and Langlade are joined by a long, thin strip of sand.
WLF: Wallis and Futuna are French islands far out in the South Pacific Ocean.
Wallis Island has round crater lakes, like Lake Lalolalo, with steep rocky sides.
MAF: Saint Martin shares its island with Sint Maarten, so one island has a French side and a Dutch side.
Its warm, clear waters are great for spotting sea turtles and tropical fish while snorkelling.
BLM: The island's airport has a very short runway, so planes swoop down over a hill to land.
Its main town, Gustavia, has a Swedish name because the island once belonged to Sweden.
PYF: Bora Bora has a bright turquoise lagoon with little huts built on stilts over the water.
Shiny black pearls are grown by oysters in French Polynesia's lagoons.
NCL: New Caledonia's lagoon is one of the largest in the world, circled by a huge coral reef.
The kagu, a grey bird that can barely fly and barks like a dog, lives only here.
ATF: King penguins and elephant seals crowd the beaches of the Crozet and Kerguelen Islands.
Kerguelen cabbage, a tough leafy plant, grows on the windswept Kerguelen Islands.
ALD: Åland is made up of thousands of small islands in the Baltic Sea, between Sweden and Finland.
Although it belongs to Finland, most people in Åland speak Swedish.
FIN: Finland is called the 'land of a thousand lakes', but it actually has many, many more.
Saunas are so loved in Finland that many homes have one of their own.
FJI: Fiji is made up of more than 300 islands in the South Pacific.
Its colourful reefs have earned Fiji the nickname 'the soft coral capital of the world'.
ETH: Legend says coffee was discovered in Ethiopia when a goat herder saw his goats dancing after eating coffee berries.
Ethiopia has its own calendar with 13 months in a year.
EST: Estonia has more than 2,000 islands along its coast.
In Estonia's bogs, wooden boardwalks let you walk across squishy wetlands.
ERI: In Asmara, there's an old petrol station built to look like an airplane.
The Dahlak Islands in the Red Sea are surrounded by coral reefs and visited by dolphins.
GNQ: Equatorial Guinea is the only country in Africa where Spanish is an official language.
Bioko Island is home to rare monkeys, like drills and black colobus monkeys.
SLV: El Salvador is the smallest country in Central America.
Pupusas, thick corn tortillas stuffed with cheese or beans, are the national dish.
EGY: The Great Pyramid of Giza is the only one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World still standing.
The Nile, one of the longest rivers on Earth, flows north through Egypt to the Mediterranean Sea.
ECU: On the Galápagos Islands, giant tortoises wander about and marine iguanas swim in the sea.
Ecuador is named after the equator, which runs right through the country.
DOM: Pico Duarte is the highest mountain in the whole Caribbean.
Larimar, a sky-blue gemstone, is found only in the Dominican Republic.
DMA: Boiling Lake is a flooded hot spring where grey water bubbles like a giant pot of soup.

DJI: Lake Assal is one of the saltiest lakes in the world and the lowest point in Africa.
Whale sharks, the biggest fish in the sea, gather in the Gulf of Tadjoura in winter.
GRL: Greenland is the largest island in the world and is part of the Kingdom of Denmark.
Polar bears, musk oxen and narwhals live in and around Greenland.
FRO: The name Faroe Islands means 'sheep islands', and woolly sheep graze all over the hills.
Lake Sørvágsvatn looks like it floats high above the ocean, thanks to a clever optical illusion.
DNK: LEGO bricks come from Denmark, and the name comes from 'leg godt', meaning 'play well'.
Hans Christian Andersen, who wrote The Little Mermaid, was from Denmark.
CZE: Sugar cubes were invented in the Czech lands, in the town of Dačice.
Prague's astronomical clock is over 600 years old, and little figures pop out when it strikes the hour.
CYN: On the Karpas Peninsula, wild donkeys wander freely across the countryside.
Loggerhead and green sea turtles lay their eggs on the sandy beaches here.
CYP: Halloumi is a squeaky cheese from Cyprus that you can grill without it melting.
An old Greek myth says the goddess Aphrodite rose from the sea foam at a rock near Paphos.
CUB: The bee hummingbird, the smallest bird in the world, lives only in Cuba.
Colourful old American cars from the 1950s still cruise the streets of Havana.
HRV: Plitvice Lakes are 16 lakes joined by waterfalls, in shades of blue and green.
Dalmatian dogs, with their black spots, are named after Dalmatia, a region of Croatia.
CIV: Lots of the world's cocoa beans, used to make chocolate, are grown in Ivory Coast.
In Taï National Park, chimpanzees use stones and chunks of wood as hammers to crack open nuts.
CRI: Sloths hang slowly from the trees in Costa Rica's rainforests.
'Pura vida', meaning 'pure life', is a cheerful saying you hear all over Costa Rica.
COD: Bonobos, close cousins of chimpanzees, live in the wild only in DR Congo.

COG: Western lowland gorillas live in the rainforests of Odzala-Kokoua National Park.
Brazzaville sits across the Congo River from Kinshasa, making them two of the closest capital cities in the world.
COM: Coelacanths, ancient fish from the time of the dinosaurs, still swim in the deep waters around the Comoros.
Lots of ylang-ylang, a sweet-smelling flower used to make perfume, is grown on these islands.
COL: Caño Cristales is nicknamed the 'river of five colours' because of red, yellow and green plants under the water.
Colombia has more kinds of birds than almost anywhere else on Earth.
CHN: The Great Wall of China snakes for thousands of kilometres over mountains and hills.
Giant pandas live in the bamboo forests of China's mountains.
MAC: Portuguese-style egg tarts, with flaky pastry and a sweet custard middle, are a famous Macau treat.
The Ruins of St. Paul's is the tall stone front of an old church, still standing on its own.
HKG: The Star Ferry has carried people across Victoria Harbour for more than 100 years.
Dim sum, small dishes like dumplings served in bamboo baskets, is a favourite meal in Hong Kong.
CHL: The Atacama Desert is one of the driest places on Earth.
Easter Island, part of Chile, has giant stone heads called moai.
TCD: Emi Koussi, in the Tibesti Mountains, is the highest mountain in the Sahara Desert.

CAF: At Dzanga Bai, a big forest clearing, lots of forest elephants gather to drink and play.
The Boali Falls are a big waterfall not far from the capital, Bangui.
CPV: The island of Fogo is one big volcano, and 'fogo' means 'fire' in Portuguese.
Cachupa, a slow-cooked stew of corn and beans, is Cape Verde's national dish.
CAN: Canada has the longest coastline of any country in the world.
Maple syrup comes from the sap of maple trees, and a maple leaf is on Canada's flag.
CMR: Cameroon is called 'Africa in miniature' because it has beaches, mountains, savannas and rainforests.
Goliath frogs, the biggest frogs in the world, live in Cameroon's rivers.
KHM: Angkor Wat is a giant ancient temple, and it even appears on Cambodia's flag.

MMR: Fishermen on Inle Lake row their boats standing up, using one leg to move the oar.
Bagan has thousands of ancient temples spread across a wide, dusty plain.
BDI: Burundi sits on the shore of Lake Tanganyika, the second-deepest lake in the world.
The royal drummers of Burundi perform while carrying giant drums on their heads.
BFA: Burkina Faso means 'land of upright people'.
In the village of Tiébélé, houses are painted with beautiful patterns by the women who live there.
BGR: In Bulgaria's Valley of Roses, pink roses are grown to make rose oil for perfumes.
A helpful germ used to make yogurt is named after Bulgaria.
BRN: Kampong Ayer is a whole village built on stilts over the water, with schools, shops and homes.
Proboscis monkeys, with big floppy noses, live in Brunei's mangrove forests.
BRA: Most of the Amazon rainforest, the largest rainforest on Earth, is in Brazil.
Rio de Janeiro's Carnival has giant parades with dancers in sparkly, feathery costumes.
BWA: The Okavango Delta is a river that spreads out into the Kalahari Desert instead of flowing to the sea.
Huge herds of elephants live in Botswana.
BIH: In Mostar, brave divers leap from the high stone Old Bridge into the river below.
Ćevapi, little grilled sausages served in soft flatbread, are a favourite food.
BOL: Salar de Uyuni is the world's largest salt flat, and after rain it turns into a giant mirror.
Lake Titicaca, shared with Peru, is one of the highest lakes in the world that boats can sail on.
BTN: The Tiger's Nest monastery clings to the side of a steep cliff high above a valley.
Bhutan's national animal is the takin, which looks like a mix between a goat and a cow.
BEN: Ganvié is a village built on stilts in a lake, where people get around by canoe.
Lions, elephants and hippos live in Pendjari National Park.
BLZ: The Great Blue Hole is a giant round underwater sinkhole that looks dark blue from above.
Cockscomb Basin Wildlife Sanctuary was the world's first park made to protect jaguars.
BEL: Belgium is famous for its chocolate and its crispy waffles.
Tintin and the Smurfs were both created by comic artists from Belgium.
BLR: European bison, the heaviest land animals in Europe, roam the ancient Białowieża Forest.
Draniki, crispy potato pancakes, are a favourite food in Belarus.
BRB: In Harrison's Cave, you ride a tram past underground streams and sparkly rock formations.
Flying fish are part of the national dish, cou-cou and flying fish.
BGD: The Sundarbans, the biggest mangrove forest in the world, is home to Bengal tigers.
Cox's Bazar has one of the longest natural sandy beaches in the world.
BHR: For hundreds of years, divers here collected beautiful pearls from the sea.
The Tree of Life is a lone green tree that has grown in the desert for hundreds of years.
BHS: On Big Major Cay, friendly pigs swim out to greet visiting boats!
Dean's Blue Hole is a deep underwater sinkhole, one of the deepest of its kind in the world.
AZE: Azerbaijan is called the 'Land of Fire', and at Yanar Dag, flames burn out of a hillside all the time.
Azerbaijani carpets are woven by hand in bright colours and patterns.
AUT: The famous composer Mozart was born in the Austrian city of Salzburg.
Eisriesenwelt is one of the biggest ice caves in the world, full of frozen ice shapes.
AUS: Koalas, which munch on eucalyptus leaves, are found in the wild only in Australia.
The Great Barrier Reef is the largest coral reef system in the world.
IOA: Every year, millions of red crabs march across Christmas Island to lay their eggs in the sea.
The Cocos (Keeling) Islands are coral atolls with turquoise lagoons and coconut palms.
HMD: Heard Island has Big Ben, an active volcano covered in glaciers.
Elephant seals, penguins and seabirds crowd the beaches of these icy islands.
NFK: Tall Norfolk Island pine trees grow here, and one is pictured on the island's flag.
Some islanders speak Norf'k, a language that mixes old English and Tahitian.
ATC: These tiny islands of sand and coral have no people living on them.
Sea turtles and dugongs swim in the warm waters of Ashmore Reef.
ARM: Lake Sevan is a huge, bright blue lake high up in the mountains.
Lavash, a thin, soft flatbread, is baked by slapping dough onto the hot walls of a clay oven.
ARG: Aconcagua is the highest mountain in all of the Americas.
The tango, a dramatic dance, grew up in the streets of Buenos Aires.
ATG: Antigua is said to have 365 beaches, one for every day of the year.
Barbuda has a huge colony of frigatebirds, whose males puff up big red throat pouches.
AGO: Kalandula Falls is one of the biggest waterfalls in Africa.
The giant sable antelope, with long curved horns, lives only in Angola and is a national symbol.
AND: Andorra is a tiny country high in the Pyrenees Mountains, between France and Spain.
Catalan is the official language here, and Andorra is the only country where that's true.
DZA: Algeria is the largest country in Africa.
In Tassili n'Ajjer, ancient rock paintings show giraffes and cattle from when the Sahara was green.
ALB: The Blue Eye is a spring of water so clear and blue that it looks like a giant eye.
Berat is nicknamed the 'city of a thousand windows'.
AFG: Band-e Amir is a chain of six deep blue lakes separated by natural walls of rock.
Kabuli pulao, rice cooked with carrots and raisins, is Afghanistan's national dish.
KAS: The Siachen Glacier is one of the longest glaciers in the world outside the polar regions.

ATA: Antarctica is the coldest, windiest and driest continent on Earth.

SXM: At Maho Beach, big planes fly so low over the sand as they land that people stand and watch.
Sint Maarten is the Dutch side of an island it shares with French Saint Martin.
TUV: Tuvalu means 'eight standing together', for its eight islands where people traditionally lived.

ENG: Stonehenge is a giant ring of standing stones built thousands of years ago.

SCT: The unicorn is Scotland's national animal.

WLS: Wales has a red dragon on its flag.

NIR: The Giant's Causeway is made of about 40,000 stone columns, many with six sides, formed by ancient lava.

GIB: The Rock of Gibraltar is home to Barbary macaques, the only wild monkeys in Europe.

UMI: These are small, faraway islands scattered across the Pacific Ocean and the Caribbean Sea.

CSI: The Coral Sea Islands are tiny reefs and sandy islands far out in the Coral Sea.
Sea turtles and seabirds use these little islands as safe places to nest.
CLP: Clipperton Island is a ring of coral around a lagoon, far out in the Pacific Ocean.
Thousands and thousands of orange land crabs scurry across this tiny island.
